summary: Ronald E. Purser is a scholar in religious studies, philosophy, and other fields who studied under Koshin Ogui in 1985. He served at Loyola University Chicago (~1991–1997) and became Professor für Management at San Francisco State University (~1997).

Ronald Egan is a sinologist who completed his Ph.D. at Harvard University (~1971–1977). He held posts at Harvard (~1977–1986), Wellesley College (~1986–1988), UC Santa Barbara (~1993–2012; emeritus ~2012), and Stanford University (~2012–2021).

Ronald Eric Emmerick worked in Iranian and Central Asian studies, Indology, and Tibetology, studying under Harold Walter Bailey (~1959–1965) and earning a Ph.D. from Oxford (~1962–1964). He taught at SOAS (~1967–1971) and was a professor at the University of Hamburg (1971–2001).

Ronald Inden is an Indologist and historian who taught Daud Ali. He spent his career at the University of Chicago (attested 2007), where he is Professor Emeritus of History and South Asian Languages and Civilizations (attested 2026).

Ronald M. Davidson works in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. He completed his Ph.D. at UC Berkeley by 1985, studying with numerous scholars and traditional teachers, and held an academic post at Fairfield University (attested 2002–2005, 2014).

Ronald Neufeldt is a scholar of religious studies and Indology. He spent his career at the University of Calgary (~1977–2006), serving as Associate Professor in Religious Studies (~1982–1990) and becoming Professor Emeritus in ~2006.

Ronald Y. Nakasone is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned his Ph.D. from the University of Wisconsin-Madison (~1973–1980). He served at the Institute of Buddhist Studies (~1988–1995) and the Pacific School of Religion (attested 1996).

Rong Geng was a scholar of sinology, history, archaeology, and linguistics. After studying at Peking University (~1922–1925), he held an academic post at Yenching University (~1926–1941) and taught Su Bai.

Rongdao Lai is a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and sinology who earned her Ph.D. at McGill University (attested 2013) under G. Victor Sōgen Hori and Robin D. S. Yates. She later served as Assistant Professor at McGill (attested 2026).

Ronit Ricci works in Indology, religious studies, and linguistics. She studied at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem (~1991–1996) and later held posts at the Australian National University (~2007–2013) and the Hebrew University of Jerusalem (~2013).

Rory Brendan Lindsay is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Toronto and completed his Ph.D. at Harvard University under the supervision of Leonard van der Kuijp.
Rory Mackenzie is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who completed doctoral studies under Peter Harvey. He has served as a teacher at International Christian College.

Rosalind Lefeber is an Indologist who completed her doctoral dissertation at the University of Toronto under supervisors Bimal Krishna Matilal and Ronald Morton Smith, and also studied under Daniel H. H. Ingalls. She later held a post at Toronto (attested 2007).

Rosalind O'Hanlon is an Indologist and historian who earned her Ph.D. from SOAS (~1977–1982). She was an Emeritus Fellow at Clare College, Cambridge (~1983), and served as Professor in Indian History and Culture at Oxford (~2001–2015).

Rosan Ikeda is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Komazawa University (1960–1964, ~1963–1969). He spent his academic career at Komazawa University (1969–2012, professor 1983–2012) and served as director at the Soto Zen Research Center (2009).

Rosane Rocher is a scholar of Indology and linguistics who earned an MA at Université libre de Bruxelles (~1955–1959) and studied under Ludo Rocher. She worked at the NFSR (1961–1970) and became a professor at the University of Pennsylvania (1970).

Rosemarie Fuchs is a specialist in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. She studied under Katia Holmes and Khenpo Tsultrim Gyamtso Rinpoche, and served as a member of the Marpa Translation Committee (attested 2000).

Rosemarie Lühr is a linguist and Indologist who completed her Promotion at Erlangen-Nuremberg (~1970–1977) and Habilitation at Regensburg (~1977–1984). She held professorships at Giessen (1990–1994) and Jena (1994–2013), and was honorary professor at Humboldt University (2013).
Rosemary Radford Ruether was a religious studies scholar who studied at Claremont School of Theology (~1958–1965). She held a post at Howard University (~1965–1975).

Rosina Pastore works in Indology and religious studies. She earned her PhD at the University of Lausanne, supervised by Maya Burger and Stefania Cavaliere while serving as an assistant, and later became an affiliated researcher at Ghent University (attested 2026).
